findings.description: S-005: the section is titled «Спрайты, изображения и ресурсы игры» and the chapter opener promises «спрайты», but pygame.sprite / Sprite / Group / spritecollide / groupcollide appeared zero times anywhere in chapter 20 -- «спрайт» was used only in the loose sense of 'a character image'. Chapter 21 then introduces pygame.sprite.Sprite, Group and groupcollide as new material, so nothing is missing from the course, but a reader here may assume «спрайт» already means the pygame class.
findings.resolution: Fixed in scripts/build_chapter_20.py: added an info callout «Спрайт здесь — это изображение, а не класс Pygame» stating that in this chapter «спрайт» means the object's image, that Pygame also has pygame.sprite.Sprite together with pygame.sprite.Group for updating and collision-checking many objects at once, and that chapter 21 covers them. Verified present once in the rebuilt 20-19-sprajty-i-assety.html.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Loads image assets with `pygame.image.load().convert_alpha()`, explains why a relative asset path is fragile, and teaches building paths from `Path(__file__).resolve().parent`.

`pygame.image.load()` already loads the image fully and preserves alpha; `.convert_alpha()` is an optimisation, not a requirement. -- Confirmed -- a PNG saved with alpha 100 loads back as Color(10,200,30,100) with the SRCALPHA flag set, before any convert call. The chapter's careful 'не обязательна технически' phrasing is exactly right.

A relative path is resolved against the process's current working directory, not the location of the source file. -- Confirmed -- `Path.cwd()/'assets'/'igrok.png'` yields /home/astra/Projects/Python_001/assets/igrok.png from the repo root and /tmp/assets/igrok.png from /tmp.
`Path(__file__).resolve().parent` gives a launch-directory-independent base. -- Confirmed -- this is the pattern the shipped project itself uses (bouncing_ball.py:29).

The problem recurs after PyInstaller packaging because the process CWD may differ from the executable's folder. -- Confirmed -- consistent with PyInstaller's documented one-file extraction behaviour, and correctly cross-referenced to 20.29.
